integrate.idea: Wave-0 Capability Inventory as a first-class plan artifact: a table with one row per user-facing control in scope (Retry, Diagnose, each restart context, Stop-summary, preview trigger) recording the exact backend function/endpoint that performs the work, its file:line on v1.2, and a verdict of EXISTS / STUB / ABSENT. The inventory is the input to wave scoping, not a side note — waves are written after it, not before.
integrate.note: Directly answers FM-01. Also de-risks FM-18 by forcing a named universe of controls.

integrate.idea: Evidence-by-transcript rule for the capability inventory: every EXISTS verdict must be backed by a pasted transcript of the capability being invoked directly (curl / CLI / REPL) against John's real v1.2 environment, showing a real observable effect. No verdict may rest on reading the code.
integrate.note: Turns 'the function exists' into 'the function works', which is the actual precondition for wiring a control.

integrate.idea: Reclassification rule with a third option: each control is 'wire it' (capability proven), 'build it' (capability absent — gets its own wave with its own acceptance criteria), or 'not available on this build' (explicitly scoped out and rendered as a named disabled state with a reason string, never as an enabled button).
integrate.note: The third option is what prevents the dead control from becoming a lying control (FM-01).

integrate.idea: Acceptance for every control wave is an end-to-end trace — click → handler → capability → observable side effect — captured as an artifact, not a bound-handler assertion. A test that only proves the handler was called is explicitly disallowed as evidence.

Typed AttachResult object carrying an explicit reason enum (unknown_session, session_ended, timeout, transport_error, unauthorized, unclassified), constructed at the innermost frame that still holds the signal and propagated upward as a value — never re-raised as a generic exception that loses type at a shared catch.
integrate.note: FM-08's root cause is type loss at the boundary, not missing copy.

integrate.idea: Induced-fault test per attach reason (bogus session ID, killed session, artificial delay past the deadline, blocked port, revoked credential), each asserting a distinct rendered string. Two reasons collapsing to one string is a wave failure, stated as such in the acceptance criteria.

Single error-rendering channel for the attach surface: one component owns error display, and the double-print test asserts exactly one occurrence of the error string in the DOM (count == 1, not >= 1). Fixing double-print by hiding one copy with CSS is explicitly disallowed.

Retry viability predicate: Retry derives from the reason enum whether a re-issuable action exists. Viable → re-issue and show what is being retried; not viable → the button renders a named 'cannot retry — <reason>' state. Retry never renders as an enabled control that re-issues nothing.

Pre-build rollup evidence gate: for each usage/time/cost rollup, paste into the plan the actual query, the row count, and one sample row taken from John's real v1.2 environment, plus the name of the accessor function each of the three render paths (dashboard, workbench tiles, session chrome) will call.
integrate.note: FM-02. One query at plan time replaces a mid-build stall.

integrate.idea: Standing rule — no number is computed inside a template. Every rendered number traces to a named accessor, and each accessor is unit-tested against a fixture with known counts. Grep for arithmetic in template files as a gate check.

Conditional scope-change rule written into the plan: if a rollup proves empty or unreachable from a render path, that wave's scope changes from 'surface' to 'aggregate + surface', with the aggregation split into its own wave rather than absorbed silently.

Explicit cost_state enum (measured / subscription_covered / free_tier / unmeasured / measurement_failed) stored alongside the numeric cost, added as an additive nullable column with existing rows defaulting to unmeasured. The representation decision is made at plan time, before any cost wave is written.
integrate.note: FM-03. Must be reconciled with the shared-artifact ledger (I43/I46) before Wave 1.

integrate.idea: Grep-able lint/test that fails on any comparison of a cost value to literal zero for labelling purposes, banning the inference 0 ⇒ subscription anywhere in the codebase. The lint is a gate command, not a convention.
Cost fixture set with one row per cost_state, with acceptance that five visibly distinct labels render — asserted on the visible text node, and reviewed by eye in the attached screenshot.

Shared tri-state conformance harness (unknown / empty / zero) that every surface wave must instantiate rather than hand-write. Seeds all three states end-to-end and asserts three distinct strings in rendered HTML, so no wave can author an assertion tailored to pass its own surface.
integrate.note: FM-04. Built once in an early wave; a dependency of every surface wave.

integrate.idea: Repo-wide lint forbidding `||` fallbacks and template `default:` filters on any value in the cost/usage/health namespace, requiring `??` or an explicit null check. Catches the class of bug where a legitimate 0 is swallowed into 'unknown'.

Null-preservation audit across the serialization stack: check that serializers, dataclass/TypedDict defaults, and ORM coercions do not fill None with 0 or '' between the accessor and the DOM. Audit output is a short table of every coercion point found, with a fix or a justification per row.
integrate.note: The API-level assertion passing while the DOM lies is FM-04's mechanism; this finds where the lie is introduced.

integrate.idea: Per-engine diagnostic depth taxonomy — credential_present / auth_round_trip / minimal_live_call / capability_probe / none — documented per engine and rendered in the UI next to the result ('Claude: live call OK', 'Grok: credentials present, not exercised'). A bare green check with no depth label is forbidden.
integrate.note: FM-07. Depth is the honest content; the checkmark alone is the lie.

integrate.idea: 'No diagnostic available' is an explicit fourth Doctor state, not a pass and not a failure. Any engine without a real diagnostic renders it, and the plan says so up front rather than discovering it mid-wave.

Forced-failure fixture per engine (wrong key, unreachable endpoint) proving the diagnostic is real: a broken credential must produce a distinguishable failure state. A check that returns green against a wrong key is a wave failure.

Typed, versioned banner→Doctor handoff payload (issue id, engine, raw signal, timestamp), with a test asserting the payload arrives at Doctor and pre-selects/pre-populates the named issue rather than dropping the user on a generic Doctor page.

Do NOT unify restart. Enumerate every context where restart is offered, name the scope in the label ('Restart run', 'Restart session', 'Restart engine', 'Restart workbench'), state per control what is preserved and what is lost, and require a scope-naming confirmation where the blast radius is large. Genuine unification becomes a separate explicit decision by John.
integrate.note: FM-10. Flags a live tension with SC-5's literal 'one restart control' wording — worth resolving with John at the Stage-1 gate.

integrate.idea: Stop-summary is designed from a persisted-state inventory taken first: what actually survives the stop (steps completed, tokens consumed, files touched, last output chunk, exit reason) is enumerated before the summary is designed. Thin honest content ('Stopped at step 3 of 8; 2 files written; partial output not retained') is an acceptable named state.

Contingency written into the plan: if the inventory shows nothing meaningful is retained at stop, the wave's real scope is 'checkpoint partial state during runs' — a larger, separately-planned wave — and the summary wave depends on it rather than papering over it.

Define 'restart quality' as a written contract per restart scope (what is re-run, what state is carried, what is discarded, what the user sees during the transition), so SC-5's 'documented and testable' clause has an object to test against instead of a vibe.

Before the preview wave, read the working new-window renderer and write down explicitly which behaviors are its own and which belong to the browser (content-type sniffing, download disposition, plugin rendering). The plan records this split; the wave scopes only what must be re-implemented inline.
integrate.note: FM-06. 'Reuse the working path' is only safe once you know what the path actually did.

integrate.idea: Explicit content-classification step in the shared preview path: magic-byte detection + declared content type + size ceiling, resolving to named states — text preview / image preview / document preview / 'binary file — N bytes, download' / 'too large to preview' / 'unsupported type — download'.

Preview acceptance fixture set: UTF-8 text, invalid-UTF-8 bytes, PNG, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, zero-byte file, and an oversized file. Raw binary rendered as text is a hard fail, asserted negatively (no control characters / replacement chars in the rendered node).

Decide the Office/PDF rendering strategy explicitly at plan time — native browser viewer, an existing conversion path already in the repo, or an honest 'download to open' state — rather than assuming inline rendering is a reuse away. Whichever is chosen, it is named in the wave with its dependency.

For projects-collapsed, determine the source of the state before writing any fix: DOM default vs. server-rendered attribute vs. persisted preference (localStorage / user row / cookie). The wave's first deliverable is the provenance finding, not a CSS change.
Version-stamped preference key (or a one-time migration) so stale stored values are ignored when the default changes — shipped with the fix, not after John reports it still broken.

Dual-profile verification standard for every UI-state fix: verified on a clean profile AND on John's existing profile with its real stored preferences. A fix verified only on a clean profile is not accepted.

Name the cadence owner in the plan — which process, its lifetime, its supervision, and what happens on restart — and confirm it against the deployment John actually runs. Where no supervised owner exists, prefer pull-on-render or a client-driven poll over a server-held timer.
integrate.note: FM-05. A timer in a recycled worker fires N times or zero and looks identical to a working one.

integrate.idea: Stamp every telemetry-derived value with an `as_of` timestamp and render staleness explicitly ('as of 4m ago' / 'stale — last update 2h ago'). A dead cadence then surfaces as a named state instead of a frozen number that looks current.
integrate.note: This is the single highest-leverage idea in the set: it converts an entire class of silent lie into a visible state, for one field.

integrate.idea: Measure, per engine, when usage/cost data actually becomes available relative to render, and design for the measured latency: a 'pending — measuring' state with an as_of stamp and a refresh, plus post-hoc reconciliation that updates the tile when the real number lands.

Practical-usefulness acceptance criterion alongside every honesty criterion: after the named reproducible task completes, the tiles must show real numbers within a stated window (e.g. 60s). A surface that renders 'unknown' perpetually is a wave failure, not a pass.
integrate.note: Guards against a perfectly honest, perfectly useless dashboard.

integrate.idea: Every failure-state table is explicitly open-ended: it carries a terminal `unclassified` state whose rendered string is honest ('Unexpected failure — <raw reason>') and whose occurrence is logged with the raw signal for later classification.
integrate.note: FM-14. Plan-time enumeration is never complete; the table must have a floor.

integrate.idea: Per-wave fault-induction step: attempt three faults not listed in that wave's table; anything producing an unclassified or misclassified state must be added to the table before the wave closes. Failure-state tables are living artifacts, amended per wave.

Strengthen UI assertions from 'string present in HTML' to 'string present in a visible text node' — element not display:none, not aria-hidden, not zero-size, not inside a collapsed container. String presence in markup is explicitly not evidence of user-visibility.

Human-verification artifact per surface wave: a screenshot or short recorded interaction attached to the EXECUTION-LOG, plus an explicit written note in the plan that the automated gate does not certify visual distinguishability — so GREEN is never overread as 'a human could tell these apart'.

Prove the frontend coverage toolchain on v1.2 before Wave 1 by producing one real coverage report. If none exists, either scope its setup as an explicit early wave or state plainly in the plan that frontend coverage is not measured and substitute a named alternative (per-handler end-to-end tests enumerated against a handler inventory). A Python coverage number may never satisfy a JS coverage criterion.

Each wave carries its own scoped pytest gate command with -v, written into the wave doc verbatim so the orchestrator runs exactly what the plan specifies — no whole-suite runs standing in for a scoped gate, no gate command invented at run time.

Shared-artifact ledger produced before Wave 1: every database/schema, config file, package manifest, static asset path, and deployed endpoint, with a recorded yes/no on whether v1.2 writes to it. Plus a per-wave checklist line — 'this wave modified these shared artifacts: ___' — requiring an empty answer or an explicit isolation note.
integrate.note: FM-09. Branch discipline does not cover shared state; this is the channel that breaks collaborators.

integrate.idea: v1.2-scoped isolates for every shared artifact that must be written: separate dev database, additive-only migrations behind a feature flag defaulted off for v1.1.x, versioned static asset paths. The isolation mechanism is named per artifact, not asserted generally.

Collaborator smoke-check protocol: after any wave that touched a shared artifact, one v1.1.x collaborator confirms their environment still works, and the result is recorded in the EXECUTION-LOG. Named person, named check, recorded outcome.

Resolve the cost_state ↔ branch-isolation interaction at plan time: confirm explicitly whether an additive nullable column plus backfill is acceptable under isolation (it usually is — additive, defaulted, unread by v1.1.x code). If it is not, state plainly that the cost honesty criterion cannot be fully met on v1.2 and scope it down, rather than meeting it cosmetically at the render layer.
integrate.note: FM-23. Two individually-satisfied constraints producing a jointly-unmet outcome is the hardest failure to see mid-build.

integrate.idea: Standing renegotiation rule for the whole plan: any criterion that becomes unachievable because of a constraint discovered mid-build is renegotiated with John explicitly, never satisfied cosmetically and never quietly dropped. The renegotiation is logged as a plan amendment.

Foreman containment smoke run before Wave 1: cwd set to planning/sleep-2026-07-28/stage2/, one trivial edit to a file at the repo root, confirm the file changed at the correct path and the run did not halt. If containment blocks it, resolve before Wave 1 (run with cwd at repo root and pass the plan by path, or relocate the plan).
integrate.note: FM-16. Five-minute check gating an eleven-wave run.

integrate.idea: Handoff hygiene as an explicit gate: doc-trio + foreman.config.json exist only under planning/sleep-2026-07-28/stage2/, root foreign artifacts are untouched (verified by a git-status diff before and after), commits land per wave, EXECUTION-LOG is appended per wave.

Attestation counts are host-computed: the orchestrator (not the sub-agent) runs the suite and writes the pass count, file paths, and test names into the EXECUTION-LOG. Each attestation names a test a third party can re-run. Any number an agent produced is stamped as a claim, not evidence.
integrate.note: FM-22. The evidence layer cannot be self-reported by the thing being evidenced.

integrate.idea: Mechanical per-wave commit cross-check: files-touched in the wave's commit vs. files-required by its acceptance criteria, diffed by the orchestrator. A wave whose commit does not touch the files its criteria name is flagged regardless of test results.

Name the reproducible verification task in the plan now — the specific project, command, and expected duration — long enough that stop/restart are meaningful and exercising all three engines so Doctor's per-engine reporting can be verified. Confirm John can run it today, before the build. Every wave's acceptance references this named task; S1 runs it end to end.
integrate.note: FM-17. Without this, every wave verifies against whatever toy the agent could summon.

integrate.idea: Define S1's mechanics in the plan before the build: who runs it, against which named task, what a failure produces, and where resulting defects go. Make the build's terminal status 'awaiting S1' rather than 'done'. An absent S1 verdict means the effort has not shipped.

Control-and-surface sweep inventory: enumerate every interactive control and every surface rendering health/usage/diagnose across the product, check each against the honesty rule even where no change is needed, and fund a late audit wave that either fixes or explicitly documents the ones outside the ten criteria.
integrate.note: FM-18/FM-24. The North Star promises 'no dead control' across John's free traversal; the criteria enumerate a subset. This closes the gap with an inventory instead of a list.

integrate.idea: Write the proxy gap into the plan explicitly: the ten criteria are a proxy for the North Star, not the North Star. Build status is reported as 'ten criteria met; North Star pending S1', and S1 is the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met, with a real free-traversal sampling protocol.
integrate.note: FM-24. Costs nothing at plan time and prevents GREEN from being read as a claim it cannot support.

integrate.idea: Rollup correctness spot-check now: hand-compute the expected token/cost/session numbers for one known session and compare against what the rollup returns. Pre-decide the policy in writing — if numbers prove wrong, do they block the wave, ship behind a 'provisional data' label, or spin out as separate work — so the choice is not made under mid-build pressure.
integrate.note: FM-21. Same query as I09; one extra column of expectation.

integrate.idea: A shared 'named state' vocabulary + render primitive: one documented set of states (measured / pending / unknown / empty / zero / unmeasured / failed / unavailable / unclassified) and one UI component that renders them consistently with distinct visual treatment. Every surface consumes it rather than inventing its own copy and styling.
integrate.note: Oranges: the real goal isn't fixing N surfaces, it's making the next surface honest by default. Also kills FM-13's 'three distinct strings, all identical grey dashes'.

integrate.idea: Traceability matrix carried as a live plan artifact: defect → criterion → wave → acceptance test → S1 check. Any row with a gap (a criterion with no test, a wave with no criterion) is visible at a glance at each gate.

Explicit wave dependency ordering baked into the plan: evidence/inventory waves first (capability inventory, rollup evidence, shared-artifact ledger, containment smoke, coverage-toolchain proof), then enabling waves (cost_state migration, tri-state harness, named-state primitive, fault-injection helper), then surface waves, then the audit/sweep wave, then S1. No surface wave may start before its enabling wave is GREEN.
integrate.note: Most of the premortem's failures are ordering failures wearing a scope costume.

integrate.idea: Shared fault-injection test utility (force timeout, force transport error, force auth failure, force empty result, force null cost) reused across the attach, Doctor, telemetry, and cost waves, so induced-fault testing is cheap enough that every wave actually does it.

Per-wave 'honesty budget' review question answered in writing before the wave closes: 'what does this surface now claim, and what is the weakest evidence behind that claim?' — a one-paragraph adversarial self-check that catches the lying-control class before the gate does.
integrate.note: Cheap; catches FM-01/FM-07/FM-11-shaped failures at authoring time.

integrate.idea: Screenshot/interaction capture tooling decided at plan time (which tool, where artifacts land, how they are referenced from EXECUTION-LOG) so the human-verification artifact in I40 is mechanically producible rather than a good intention that dies in Wave 2.

EXECUTION-LOG schema fixed up front: per wave — criteria addressed, gate command run, host-computed pass count, test names, files touched, shared artifacts modified, screenshots, faults induced, new states added to tables, collaborator smoke result. A schema makes an under-delivering wave structurally visible instead of prose-visible.
integrate.note: Directly attacks FM-22's 'a half-done wave produces an identical-looking log'.

grasscatcher.idea: Full observability stack (OpenTelemetry, metrics backend, tracing) for Anchor telemetry instead of as_of stamps and pull-on-render.
grasscatcher.note: Would serve SC-8 incidentally but is an infrastructure program, not a defect-honesty effort. Park it.

grasscatcher.idea: Dashboard visual redesign / design-system overhaul so the honest states look good.
grasscatcher.note: The named-state primitive (I57) covers the minimum needed for distinguishability; a redesign is separate work.

grasscatcher.idea: Cost budgeting, spend caps, and alerting built on top of the new cost_state data.
grasscatcher.note: Natural sequel once cost is honest; not required by any criterion.

grasscatcher.idea: Historical usage analytics and time-series charts over the rollups.
Migrating the frontend to a component framework to make state rendering cleaner.
grasscatcher.note: Tempting while touching every surface; would swamp the effort and multiply FM-09's shared-artifact risk.

grasscatcher.idea: Provider abstraction refactor / adding a fourth engine behind a uniform diagnostic interface.
grasscatcher.note: The depth taxonomy (I18) gets the honesty benefit without the refactor.

grasscatcher.idea: Backfilling historical cost from provider invoices so old rows stop reading 'unmeasured'.
grasscatcher.note: 'unmeasured' on historical rows is the honest answer; backfill is an optional later nicety.

grasscatcher.idea: Real-time WebSocket push infrastructure to replace polling for live tiles.
grasscatcher.note: SC-8 needs a proven owner and an as_of stamp, not a transport upgrade.

grasscatcher.idea: A general document-conversion microservice (LibreOffice/Gotenberg) for the product at large.
grasscatcher.note: Distinct from I29, which picks the minimum viable strategy for the preview path only.

grasscatcher.idea: Internationalization of the new state strings.
Performance optimization of the dashboard render path encountered while adding accessors.
grasscatcher.note: Likely to be noticed mid-build; pre-parking it prevents an unplanned fork.

dropped.idea: Porting the honesty fixes back to the v1.1.x line so collaborators benefit too.
dropped.note: Directly contradicts the North Star's isolation clause ('Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators'). Named here so it is refused explicitly rather than drifted into.
